docs.title: vexy-speakup
docs.text:
vexy-speakup restores a recorded conversation with the VST3 speech plugins you already have installed. It works one speaker at a time, levels each speaker, masters the whole recording, and gives you back the same file type. If the input is a video, the original video packets are copied unchanged and only the audio track is replaced, so the timeline stays exactly as it was.

vexy-speakup run meeting.mp4 --profile_name=dx65 --verbose

For meeting.mp4, this writes meeting_improved.mp4 beside the input and keeps every intermediate file in a new run folder under meeting/.

docs.title: What happens to a recording
docs.text:
1. FFmpeg decodes the first audio stream to 48 kHz stereo 32-bit float WAV.
  2. A local diarizer labels who speaks when. You can also supply your own speaker turns as JSON.
  3. The timeline is split into disjoint intervals: one speaker, several speakers at once (overlap), or nobody (background).
  4. Each speaker's fragments go through that speaker's VST3 chain in an isolated worker process.
  5. Each speaker gets a loudness baseline, and each fragment is corrected within 3 dB of it.
  6. The fragments are written back onto the original timeline, sample for sample.
  7. The whole recording is levelled to EBU R128, sent through the master chain, and levelled again to the target loudness and true peak.
  8. The result is encoded and checked for true peak. For video, the new audio is remuxed with the original video.

How processing works follows a single recording through these steps in detail.

docs.title: Requirements at a glance
docs.text:
• macOS, Python 3.12 or later, and ffmpeg/ffprobe on PATH.
  • Installed VST3 plugins. The built-in profiles expect Accentize dxRevive Pro, iZotope RX 12 Voice De-noise and iZotope Ozone 12 Maximizer.
  • For automatic diarization, optional DeepFilterNet restoration and quality scoring: the local model adapters described in Local models. Without them, supply speaker turns with --diarization_json and turn scoring off with --evaluate=False.

No plugin, model or recording is distributed with the package, and nothing is uploaded anywhere.

docs.text: Page Read it when you want to Installation install the tool and check prerequisites Quickstart process a first recording Command reference look up every command and flag Profiles and custom chains choose or write plugin chains How processing works understand levels, overlap and timing Run folders and reports find and read the files a run leaves behind Local models set up diarization, DeepFilterNet and scoring Troubleshooting fix a failed run Development test, build and release the package

• Ported the speech-polish script collection into the installable vexy_speakup package with a vexy-speakup command-line tool.
  • Versions come from git tags through hatch-vcs. Added a version command.
  • Plugin workers run as python -m vexy_speakup, so the installed package needs no script beside it.
  • Replaced machine-specific paths: plugins default to /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3 (VEXY_SPEAKUP_PLUGIN_ROOT), and local model adapters come from VEXY_SPEAKUP_TTS_ROOT, looked up only when used.
  • Folded the standalone plugin probe script into the probe command.
  • Added build.sh and publish.sh.

The full history is in CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text:
vexy-speakup is a Fire command-line tool. Flags use underscores, as in --profile_name, and Boolean flags take an explicit value, as in --evaluate=False. Add --help after a command to print its flags:

vexy-speakup run --help
Command Purpose run process an audio or video file attempts process one excerpt with several profiles for comparison inspect list a plugin's controls and their ranges probe load one plugin, record its controls and render a test signal inventory list the VST3 bundles in the plugin folder version print the installed package version

docs.title: run
docs.text:
vexy-speakup run INPUT_PATH [flags]

Processes an audio or video file and prints the output path.

Flag Default Meaning --work_dir input path without its extension folder that receives a new run folder --output_path input name plus --suffix output file; its extension selects the format --suffix _improved added to the input name when --output_path is empty --profile_name dx35 built-in plugin profile: dx35, dx65, rx6-dx35, rx6 or bypass --config_path empty JSON file with custom chains; replaces the profile --diarizer mlx mlx or sortformer --diarization_json empty speaker turns to use instead of a diarizer --target_lufs -16 integrated loudness target, from -70 to -5 LUFS --true_peak -2 true-peak ceiling, from -9 to 0 dBTP --max_chunk 30 longest processed interval, in seconds --start 0 excerpt start, in seconds (audio input only) --duration 0 excerpt length, in seconds; 0 means to the end (audio input only) --evaluate True score matching before/after windows --metrics_python empty Python interpreter of the scoring environment --ai none none, or deepfilter to run DeepFilterNet3 before the VSTs --timeout 1800 time limit, in seconds, for each external process --force False replace an existing output file --verbose False print each stage

The command checks its arguments before it starts work:

  • All numbers must be finite; --start and --duration must not be negative; --max_chunk and --timeout must be positive.
  • The input file, the output file and the work folder must all be different.
  • An existing output is refused unless --force is given.
  • A video input cannot be combined with --start or --duration.
  • A --config_path file must contain speech and master arrays.

docs.title: Output names
docs.text:
With no --output_path, the output goes beside the input:

Input Output Work folder talk.mp4 talk_improved.mp4 talk/ talk.m4a talk_improved.m4a talk/ talk.m4a with --start or --duration talk_improved_preview.m4a talk/

docs.title: Output formats
docs.text:
The output extension selects the audio codec:

Extension Codec .wav 24-bit PCM, little-endian .aif, .aiff 24-bit PCM, big-endian .flac FLAC .mp3 MP3 (LAME), 192 kb/s .ogg, .opus, .webm Opus, 192 kb/s anything else AAC, 192 kb/s

docs.title: Export audio from a video
docs.text:
If the input has a video stream and the output extension is an audio-only format (.wav, .mp3, .m4a, .aac, .flac, .ogg, .opus, .aif, .aiff, .caf, .wma or .ac3), the result is audio only:

vexy-speakup run meeting.mp4 --output_path=speech.wav

An embedded cover image does not count as a video stream.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Explicit paths and loudness
vexy-speakup run meeting.mp4 \
  --work_dir=work --output_path=result.mp4 \
  --target_lufs=-16 --true_peak=-2 --verbose

# Local DeepFilterNet3 CoreML pass before the VST chain
vexy-speakup run meeting.m4a --ai=deepfilter

# Reuse earlier or corrected speaker turns instead of running a diarizer
vexy-speakup run meeting.m4a --diarization_json=turns.json

# Sortformer diarizer (up to four speakers)
vexy-speakup run meeting.m4a --diarizer=sortformer

# Custom chains
vexy-speakup run meeting.m4a --config_path=custom-chain.json

docs.title: attempts
docs.text:
vexy-speakup attempts INPUT_PATH [flags]

Processes one excerpt with several profiles and keeps every result for listening. It prints the path of comparison.json.

Flag Default Meaning --work_dir <input name>_attempts beside the input folder for all attempts --start 120 excerpt start, in seconds --duration 45 excerpt length, in seconds --profiles dx35,dx65,rx6-dx35 comma-separated profile names --metrics_python empty Python interpreter of the scoring environment --verbose True print each stage

The command extracts the excerpt to sample.wav, diarizes it once with the mlx diarizer, and writes turns.json. It then runs run once per profile with those turns, writing <profile>.wav and a <profile>/ work folder. Finally it collects every run's report into comparison.json.

attempts always uses the mlx diarizer, so it needs VEXY_SPEAKUP_TTS_ROOT.

docs.title: inspect
docs.text:
vexy-speakup inspect PLUGIN_PATH [--output_path=FILE]

Loads a plugin the same way a chain does and prints JSON with its name, reported latency, current parameter values and the range of each parameter. Use it to find the exact parameter names before you write a custom chain. With --output_path, the JSON is also saved to that file. A licence or loading problem appears as an error.

vexy-speakup inspect /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/Accentize-dxRevivePro.vst3

docs.title: probe
docs.text:
vexy-speakup probe PLUGIN_PATH OUTPUT_PATH [--audio_path=FILE]

Loads one plugin directly and writes OUTPUT_PATH as JSON with:

  • each control's value, raw value, range and valid values,
  • the number of input and output frames of a test render,
  • whether every output sample is finite, and the output peak.

Without --audio_path, the test signal is one second of stereo silence at 48 kHz. With it, the file is read instead. Two seconds of silence are added to the end in both cases. The command prints the plugin name, the number of parameters and the output shape.

vexy-speakup probe /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/Accentize-dxRevivePro.vst3 probe.json

docs.title: inventory
docs.text:
vexy-speakup inventory [--output_path=inventory.json]

Finds every .vst3 bundle under the plugin folder without loading any plugin. It writes the folder, the count and the sorted bundle paths to --output_path (default inventory.json) and prints the count. The plugin folder is /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3 unless VEXY_SPEAKUP_PLUGIN_ROOT is set.

docs.title: version
docs.text:
vexy-speakup version

Prints the installed package version.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Effect VEXY_SPEAKUP_PLUGIN_ROOT plugin folder for built-in profiles and inventory VEXY_SPEAKUP_TTS_ROOT folder with the local model adapters

run also sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 for itself and its child processes, so model access never reaches the network.

docs.title: Profiles and custom chains
docs.text:
A chain is an ordered list of VST3 plugins. vexy-speakup uses two kinds:

  • Speech chains process each speaker's fragments separately. The plugin state is reset between fragments.
  • The master chain processes the whole assembled recording continuously, after the speakers have been levelled and put back on the timeline.

You choose chains with a built-in profile (--profile_name) or a JSON file (--config_path). A file replaces the profile completely.

docs.title: Built-in profiles
docs.text:
Profile Speech chain Master chain dx35 (default) dxRevive Pro, mix 35% Ozone 12 Maximizer dx65 dxRevive Pro, mix 65% Ozone 12 Maximizer rx6-dx35 RX 12 Voice De-noise at 6 dB, then dxRevive Pro at 35% Ozone 12 Maximizer rx6 RX 12 Voice De-noise at 6 dB Ozone 12 Maximizer bypass none none

dx35 is the conservative choice. dx65 led DNSMOS on the Zoom excerpt it was tested on. bypass skips every plugin but still performs the level passes, which makes it a useful reference when you compare attempts.

The profiles set these plugin parameters:

Plugin bundle Parameters Accentize-dxRevivePro.vst3 mix = 35.0 or 65.0, bypass = false RX 12 Voice De-noise.vst3 reduction = 6.0, adaptive_mode = true, global_bypass = false Ozone 12 Maximizer.vst3 max_output_level = -2.0, max_input_gain_db = 0.0, max_upward_compression_amt_db = 0.0, max_soft_clip_on_off = false, global_bypass = false

The bundles are loaded from /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3, or from VEXY_SPEAKUP_PLUGIN_ROOT if it is set. The parameter names were verified against the locally installed plugin versions; a different plugin version may name its controls differently.

docs.title: Custom chain files
docs.text:
A chain file is a JSON object with three keys:

Key Type Meaning speech array of plugin entries default chain for every speaker speakers object, optional chains for individual speaker IDs; each replaces speech for that speaker master array of plugin entries continuous chain after assembly

speech and master are required. Either may be an empty array.

Each plugin entry accepts:

Field Required Meaning path yes path to the .vst3 bundle; ~ is expanded parameters no object of parameter names and values plugin_name no which plugin to load from a bundle that contains several preset no path to a .vstpreset file loaded before parameters are applied

Every parameter name is checked against the loaded plugin. An unknown name stops the run with an error that suggests inspect. Every plugin must be an effect. Saved presets should come from your own host and the installed plugin version.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The repository includes examples/custom-chain.example.json:

{
  "speech": [
    {
      "path": "/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/Accentize-dxRevivePro.vst3",
      "parameters": {"mix": 65.0, "bypass": false}
    }
  ],
  "speakers": {
    "0": [
      {
        "path": "/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/RX 12 Mouth De-click.vst3",
        "parameters": {"sensitivity": 3.0, "output_clicks_only": false, "global_bypass": false}
      },
      {
        "path": "/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/Accentize-dxRevivePro.vst3",
        "parameters": {"mix": 35.0, "bypass": false}
      }
    ]
  },
  "master": [
    {
      "path": "/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/Ozone 12 Maximizer.vst3",
      "parameters": {"max_output_level": -2.0, "max_input_gain_db": 0.0, "global_bypass": false}
    }
  ]
}

With this file, speaker 0 gets mouth de-clicking and a lighter dxRevive mix of 35%. Every other speaker gets dxRevive at 65%. The master chain is the Ozone Maximizer.

Speaker IDs are the labels in the speaker turns: whatever the diarizer produced, or the speaker values in your --diarization_json file. Overlap intervals use the shared speech chain, because they belong to no single speaker.

docs.title: Write a chain for your plugins
docs.text:
1. List the installed bundles:

    vexy-speakup inventory --output_path=inventory.json

  2. Print the controls of the plugin you want to use:

    vexy-speakup inspect "/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/RX 12 Mouth De-click.vst3"

    The parameters object shows each control's current value, and ranges shows its range.

  3. Copy examples/custom-chain.example.json to custom-chain.json and edit the paths and parameter names to match the inspect output.

  4. Test the chain on an audio excerpt:

    vexy-speakup run meeting.m4a --config_path=custom-chain.json \
  --start=120 --duration=45

  5. Open the run folder and check speakers/<ID>/vst-receipt.json. It records the parameter values each plugin actually used.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-speakup.git
cd vexy-speakup

  2. Run the tests. uv creates the environment with the test extra:

    ./test.sh

    test.sh runs pytest with coverage of vexy_speakup, then ruff check on src and tests.

The functional tests encode real audio and video with FFmpeg, so ffmpeg and ffprobe must be on PATH. Tests that need licensed plugins or the local model adapters cannot run without them.

docs.title: Source layout
docs.text:
Module Responsibility cli.py the Fire commands, argument checks and the run pipeline media.py FFmpeg decoding, loudness measurement, encoding and atomic publication models.py diarization, DeepFilterNet and scoring through local adapters turns.py turn validation and timeline partitioning levels.py BS.1770 loudness and bounded gain pipeline.py fragment extraction, speaker rendering, levelling, assembly and mastering vst.py built-in profiles, chain loading and VST rendering audit.py inspect, probe, inventory, attempts and evaluation windows locations.py plugin and adapter folders from environment variables

Plugin rendering runs in child processes started as python -m vexy_speakup _render and python -m vexy_speakup _master. These internal commands read a job JSON file and are not meant to be called by hand.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
./build.sh            # documentation and package
./build.sh docs       # documentation only
./build.sh package    # package only

The package step removes dist/, runs uv build and checks the result with twine check. The version comes from the git tag through hatch-vcs and is written to src/vexy_speakup/__version__.py, which git ignores. An untagged commit builds a development version, which PyPI does not accept.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation source is in src_docs/md/, and src_docs/mkdocs.yml configures ProperDocs with the MaterialX theme. Build it with:

src_docs/build.sh          # strict build into docs/
src_docs/build.sh serve    # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000

The site is built into docs/, which GitHub Pages serves at https://vexy.dev/vexy-speakup/. A push to main that changes src_docs/ rebuilds docs/ through the Docs workflow.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
./publish.sh

publish.sh runs uvx gitnextver, which commits pending changes, creates the next vX.Y.Z tag and pushes. It stops if HEAD then carries no such tag. It then builds the package from that tag and uploads it with uv publish. A credential such as UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN must be set.

Run ./test.sh before you publish; publish.sh does not run the tests.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• macOS. The package metadata lists macOS as its operating system, and the default plugin folder is the macOS system VST3 folder.
  • Python 3.12 or later.
  • uv to install the command-line tool.
  • FFmpeg with ffprobe, both on PATH. FFmpeg decodes, measures loudness, encodes and remuxes video.
  • The VST3 plugins your chain uses, installed and licensed on this machine.

docs.title: Install the tool
docs.text:
1. Install the package as a uv tool:

    uv tool install vexy-speakup

    To install from a source checkout instead, run this in the repository folder:

    uv tool install .

  2. Check that the command is available:

    vexy-speakup version

    The command prints the installed package version.

  3. Check that FFmpeg is available:

    ffmpeg -version
ffprobe -version

docs.title: Python dependencies
docs.text:
The package installs these libraries:

Library Used for fire the command-line interface numpy sample buffers, gains and fades pedalboard==0.9.26 hosting VST3 plugins, with latency compensation soundfile streaming float and RF64 WAV files pyloudnorm BS.1770 loudness of speakers and fragments

Pedalboard is pinned to 0.9.26 because plugin rendering was verified with that exact wheel.

docs.title: Plugin folder
docs.text:
The built-in profiles load plugins from /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3. To use another folder, set VEXY_SPEAKUP_PLUGIN_ROOT:

export VEXY_SPEAKUP_PLUGIN_ROOT="$HOME/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3"
vexy-speakup inventory --output_path=inventory.json

inventory lists every .vst3 bundle under that folder without loading any plugin, so it is a quick way to check the folder setting.

The variable affects the built-in profiles and inventory. A custom chain file uses the full path written in each plugin entry.

docs.title: Local model adapters
docs.text:
Automatic diarization, the optional DeepFilterNet pass and quality scoring call local adapters that live outside this package. Point VEXY_SPEAKUP_TTS_ROOT at the folder that holds them:

export VEXY_SPEAKUP_TTS_ROOT=/path/to/tts

Local models lists what the folder must contain. You can process recordings without it by supplying speaker turns and turning scoring off:

vexy-speakup run meeting.m4a --diarization_json=turns.json --evaluate=False

docs.title: Local models
docs.text: Diarization, DeepFilterNet restoration and quality scoring are not Python dependencies of vexy-speakup. They call local adapters and native hosts that run in their own uv environments. All model access runs offline, with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, and no paid service is used.

docs.title: The adapter folder
docs.text:
Set VEXY_SPEAKUP_TTS_ROOT to the folder that holds myasr/, myaud/ and .external/:

export VEXY_SPEAKUP_TTS_ROOT=/path/to/tts

The folder is only looked up when a feature needs it. If it is unset or is not a folder, that feature stops with an error that names the variable.

Feature Files used under VEXY_SPEAKUP_TTS_ROOT mlx diarizer myasr/tools/diarize-mlx.py sortformer diarizer .external/NeMo-Speech.cpp/build/metal-asr/bin/nemo-speech --ai=deepfilter myaud/catalogs/deepfilternet-coreml.json, .cache/issue201/deepfilternet-coreml-materialized/, .external/DeepFilterNet-mlx/ evaluation myaud/tools/aud-metrics.py

docs.title: mlx (default)
docs.text: Runs myasr/tools/diarize-mlx.py with uv run --offline --script in offline mode. It uses the cached mlx-community/Nemotron-3-Diarization-8bit conversion and processes the complete file with its own bounded context, so speaker IDs are not restarted per fragment. The raw result goes to diarization-native/report.json in the run folder.

docs.title: sortformer
docs.text:
vexy-speakup run meeting.m4a --diarizer=sortformer

Runs the native nemo-speech diarize host on Metal with the Q8 GGUF of nvidia/diar_streaming_sortformer_4spk-v2 from the Hugging Face cache in ~/.cache/huggingface/hub. This model has four speaker slots.

Sortformer reports its last 80 ms frame as extending past the end of the file. Only that last frame is clipped to the audio duration, and the original end time is kept as end_before_eof_clip in diarization-native.json.

docs.title: Supplied turns
docs.text:
--diarization_json skips the diarizer. The file may be:

  • a list of {"start", "end", "speaker"} objects,
  • an object with a turns array, such as a turns.json from an earlier run, or
  • an object with a segments array, such as a native diarizer report.

Use this to reuse a diarization, or to correct one by editing its turns.json.

docs.title: DeepFilterNet3
docs.text: --ai=deepfilter runs DeepFilterNet3 through its CoreML host on the CPU before the VST chains. Before running, the tool checks the SHA-256 of the host binary and of every model file against myaud/catalogs/deepfilternet-coreml.json. Any mismatch stops the run. The host writes mono output, which is converted back to 48 kHz stereo float; the sample count must match the input exactly.

docs.title: Quality scoring
docs.text:
Evaluation runs myaud/tools/aud-metrics.py score with DNSMOS and UTMOS, two no-reference ONNX predictors. The interpreter is taken from:

  1. --metrics_python, if given, or
  2. the first aud-metrics-* environment under ~/.cache/uv/environments-v2.

If neither exists, or a predictor fails, the error is stored for that window in evaluation.json and the run continues. A missing predictor never becomes a synthetic score.

To skip scoring, use --evaluate=False.

docs.title: Working without the adapters
docs.text:
Everything except diarization, DeepFilterNet and scoring works without VEXY_SPEAKUP_TTS_ROOT:

vexy-speakup run meeting.m4a --diarization_json=turns.json --evaluate=False

attempts always runs the mlx diarizer, so it needs the adapters.

docs.title: Run folders and reports
docs.text:
Each run creates a new run folder inside the work folder. Earlier runs and the original file are never overwritten, so you can compare attempts or inspect a failure later.

meeting/                              work folder (default: input name without extension)
├── latest.json                       points to the last successful run
└── run-20260101-101500-123456/       one folder per run
    ├── report.json
    ├── input.wav
    ├── turns.json
    ├── fragments.json
    ├── speaker-gains.json
    ├── assembled.wav
    ├── premaster.wav
    ├── master-vst.wav
    ├── master.wav
    ├── evaluation.json
    ├── speakers/
    │   ├── 0/
    │   │   ├── jobs.json
    │   │   ├── jobs.log
    │   │   ├── vst-receipt.json
    │   │   ├── 000001-context.wav
    │   │   ├── 000001-render.wav
    │   │   ├── 000001.wav
    │   │   └── 000001-mastered.wav
    │   ├── _overlap/
    │   └── _background/
    └── evaluation/

The run folder name is the local start time with microseconds: run-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-ffffff.

A long recording can need tens of gigabytes of work files. Delete run folders you no longer need.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
File Contents report.json inputs, settings, status, levels, evaluation and publication details turns.json the validated speaker turns used for the run fragments.json every interval with original times, sample offsets, speakers, owner and gain speaker-gains.json the baseline gain of each speaker, in dB evaluation.json before/after scores for each evaluation window ../latest.json path of the last successful run folder and its report.json

report.json is written when the run starts with "status": "running". It is updated to "complete" with the results, or to "failed" with an error message. A failed run keeps all its work files.

Fields of report.json:

Field Meaning input, input_sha256 input path and its SHA-256 output output path video, output_video whether the input has video, and whether the output keeps it profile, config profile name and the full chain configuration used ai none or deepfilter preview_start the --start value target_lufs, true_peak level targets status, error run state, and the error message of a failed run duration_s decoded duration in seconds fragments number of intervals speakers sorted speaker IDs overlap_s total seconds with more than one speaker levels loudnorm measurements before and after the premaster and final passes evaluation the evaluation rows, when --evaluate=True publication codec, encoded loudness, extra codec gain and output SHA-256

docs.title: Receipts and logs
docs.text: File Contents speakers/<ID>/vst-receipt.json each plugin's path, name, reported latency and every parameter value used master-receipt.json the same for the master chain, plus the rendered frame count speakers/<ID>/jobs.json, master-job.json the job description passed to each worker speakers/<ID>/jobs.log, master.log worker output diarization.log diarizer output diarization-native/ or diarization-native.json raw diarizer result (mlx or sortformer) deepfilter.log, deepfilter-receipt.json DeepFilterNet output and model checks, with --ai=deepfilter

docs.title: Audio files
docs.text:
File Format Contents input.wav float decoded input deepfilter.wav float DeepFilterNet output, with --ai=deepfilter speakers/<ID>/NNNNNN-context.wav float fragment with up to 0.5 s of context on each side speakers/<ID>/NNNNNN-render.wav float the context file after the speech chain speakers/<ID>/NNNNNN.wav float levelled fragment, exactly as placed on the timeline speakers/<ID>/NNNNNN-mastered.wav 24-bit PCM the same interval cut from the final master assembled.wav float all fragments on the original timeline premaster.wav float assembled audio after the first loudness pass master-vst.wav float after the master chain master.wav float final levelled master

NNNNNN is the interval index in fragments.json. Background intervals get only -context.wav and the timeline .wav file.

Intermediate float files may exceed 0 dBFS. Only master.wav, the -mastered.wav cuts and the published output are peak-controlled.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: Recordings, turn files and run folders contain your private data. Keep them outside any public source tree. They are excluded from the package's source and wheel builds, and the tool uploads nothing.

docs.title: How processing works
docs.text:
This page follows one recording through vexy-speakup run. The example is a 60-second video, call.mp4, with two speakers, A and B:

Time (s) Who speaks 0.0 – 2.0 nobody 2.0 – 40.0 A 38.0 – 40.0 A and B 40.0 – 58.0 B 58.0 – 60.0 nobody

docs.title: 1. Decode
docs.text: FFmpeg decodes the first audio stream to input.wav: 48 kHz, stereo, 32-bit float, RF64 when the file is large. For video, FFmpeg resamples against the container timestamps, so audio that starts late in the video becomes leading silence. Without that, the processed audio would drift against the picture.

docs.title: 2. Diarize
docs.text:
The diarizer reads the complete input.wav, so speaker IDs stay consistent across the whole recording. The result is a list of turns, each with start, end and speaker, saved as turns.json. Diarization always sees the original signal, even when --ai=deepfilter is used.

The turns are checked before use. Each start and end must be a finite number, 0 <= start < end, and the end must lie within the audio. Each speaker ID must contain only letters, digits, _ and -.

docs.title: 3. Optional AI restoration
docs.text: With --ai=deepfilter, DeepFilterNet3 runs through its local CoreML host on the decoded audio. Its output is converted back to the same format and must have exactly the same number of samples; if not, the run stops.

docs.title: 4. Partition the timeline
docs.text:
The timeline is cut wherever a turn starts or ends. Each piece is labelled with the speakers active in it, and neighbouring pieces with the same speakers are merged. Pieces longer than --max_chunk seconds (default 30) are split. For the example, this gives:

Interval (s) Speakers Owner 0 – 2 none _background 2 – 32 A A 32 – 38 A A 38 – 40 A, B _overlap 40 – 58 B B 58 – 60 none _background

The A interval from 2 to 38 seconds is longer than 30 seconds, so it is split at 32. Every sample belongs to exactly one interval, so nothing is processed twice.

For each interval, half a second of context is cut on each side, where available, and saved as speakers/<owner>/NNNNNN-context.wav. The context gives plugins a run-up and is removed again later.

docs.title: 5. Render each speaker
docs.text:
Each owner with speech (A, B and _overlap) gets one worker process that loads its chain once: the owner's chain from speakers in a custom chain file, or the shared speech chain. Background intervals are not rendered.

For each fragment, the worker:

  1. resets the plugin state,
  2. adds two seconds of silence so plugin buffers drain,
  3. renders the fragment in stereo, with plugin latency compensated by Pedalboard,
  4. crops the result to the original length and saves it as NNNNNN-render.wav.

A render fails if it returns the wrong shape or non-finite samples, or if a non-silent input comes back silent. A silent output usually means an unlicensed plugin or a wrong setting.

Running each owner in its own process means that a plugin crash or hang stops only that worker, and --timeout limits how long it may take.

docs.title: 6. Level the speakers
docs.text:
Each rendered fragment is measured with BS.1770 integrated loudness. Fragments shorter than 400 ms are padded with silence for the measurement only.

  1. Speaker baseline. For each owner, the median loudness of its fragments, weighted by fragment length, sets a gain that brings that speaker to two LU below --target_lufs. Short turns therefore do not dominate. The baseline gain is limited to ±12 dB.
  2. Fragment correction. Each fragment may then differ from its speaker's baseline by at most 3 dB, and the total gain is limited to ±12 dB.
  3. Silence. A fragment whose RMS level is below 10⁻⁶ gets no gain, so room tone and silence are never amplified.

The gains are saved in speaker-gains.json and per fragment in fragments.json.

docs.title: 7. Assemble
docs.text: The fragments are written in timeline order to assembled.wav. The context margins are cropped away, and each processed fragment is blended with the original over 10 ms at both ends to avoid clicks. Background intervals are copied from the source unchanged. If the assembled file has a different number of samples from the input, the run stops.

docs.title: 8. Master
docs.text:
1. The assembled audio gets a two-pass EBU R128 loudnorm to --target_lufs and --true_peak (premaster.wav).
  2. The master chain processes the whole file in 10-second blocks without resetting between blocks, then drains the plugin tail (master-vst.wav).
  3. A second two-pass loudnorm sets the final loudness and true peak (master.wav).

A silent file skips loudnorm, because its loudness is undefined.

From master.wav, each speech interval is cut again as a 24-bit NNNNNN-mastered.wav, so the fragments carry the final levels.

docs.title: 9. Evaluate
docs.text: With --evaluate=True, up to three windows of up to 30 seconds are chosen, starting at the first, middle and last turn. Each window is cut from the original and from the master, and both are scored with DNSMOS and UTMOS. Missing predictors are recorded as errors in the report; they never produce invented scores. See Local models.

docs.title: 10. Encode and publish
docs.text:
The master is encoded to the output format. For a video, the original video and subtitle streams are copied without re-encoding, and the new audio replaces the old. Metadata is copied from the input.

Lossy encoders can push the true peak above the limit, so the encoded file is measured. If its true peak exceeds --true_peak by more than 0.1 dB, the volume is lowered by the excess plus 0.15 dB and the file is encoded again. The file is encoded at most three times. The output is first written to a hidden temporary file beside the destination and then renamed, so an interrupted run never leaves a half-written output.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• During overlap, the speakers are processed together as one mixed fragment. Separating simultaneous voices would need separate microphone tracks or a tested separation model.
  • Predictor scores guide comparisons. They do not establish speaker accuracy, transcript preservation or perceived quality across a whole meeting.
  • Speaker IDs are anonymous until you label them.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This walk-through processes a meeting recording called meeting.mp4. It first compares three profiles on a short excerpt, then processes the full file with the one that sounds best.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• vexy-speakup, ffmpeg and ffprobe are installed. See Installation.
  • The plugins used by the built-in profiles are installed: Accentize dxRevive Pro, iZotope RX 12 Voice De-noise and iZotope Ozone 12 Maximizer.
  • VEXY_SPEAKUP_TTS_ROOT points to the local model adapters. If you do not have them, skip to Process without local models.

docs.title: Compare profiles on an excerpt
docs.text:
1. Run attempts on the recording:

    vexy-speakup attempts meeting.mp4

    By default this takes 45 seconds starting at 120 seconds, diarizes that excerpt once, and processes it with the dx35, dx65 and rx6-dx35 profiles. Everything goes into meeting_attempts/ beside the input.

  2. Listen to meeting_attempts/dx35.wav, meeting_attempts/dx65.wav and meeting_attempts/rx6-dx35.wav.

  3. Optionally, read meeting_attempts/comparison.json. It holds the full report of each attempt, including the DNSMOS and UTMOS scores of matching windows before and after processing.

The scores help you compare attempts. They do not prove that one attempt sounds better across the whole meeting, so let your ears decide.

docs.title: Process the full recording
docs.text:
1. Run the profile you chose on the whole file:

    vexy-speakup run meeting.mp4 --profile_name=dx65 --verbose

    --verbose prints each stage as it starts. The first line names the run folder:

    Work: /path/to/meeting/run-20260101-101500-123456

  2. Wait for the final line:

    Output: /path/to/meeting_improved.mp4

    meeting_improved.mp4 contains the original video packets and the improved audio track.

  3. To read what was done, open report.json in the run folder. See Run folders and reports.

If you run the same command again, it stops because meeting_improved.mp4 already exists. Add --force to replace it. Each run creates a new run folder, so the earlier run stays available.

docs.title: Process without local models
docs.text:
Without VEXY_SPEAKUP_TTS_ROOT, give the tool your own speaker turns and turn off scoring.

  1. Write turns.json with one entry per turn. Times are in seconds from the start of the recording; speaker IDs may contain letters, digits, _ and -:

    [
  {"start": 0.0, "end": 12.4, "speaker": "anna"},
  {"start": 12.4, "end": 30.0, "speaker": "ben"},
  {"start": 28.5, "end": 41.0, "speaker": "anna"}
]

  2. Run the tool with these turns:

    vexy-speakup run meeting.m4a --diarization_json=turns.json --evaluate=False

    The result is meeting_improved.m4a. Between 28.5 and 30.0 seconds both speakers talk at once, so that interval is processed once as a mixed fragment rather than twice.

docs.title: Preview an audio file
docs.text:
For an audio input, --start and --duration process only an excerpt:

vexy-speakup run meeting.m4a --start=120 --duration=45

The output gets a _preview suffix, meeting_improved_preview.m4a, so it does not collide with a full-length output. Video input cannot be previewed this way; trim the video first, or extract the audio as shown in Command reference.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: When a run fails, start with report.json in the newest run folder. Its status is failed and error holds the message. The log files next to it contain the output of each external process; see Run folders and reports.

docs.title: Output exists: ...; use --force
docs.text: The output file is already there. Add --force to replace it, or choose another name with --output_path or --suffix.

docs.title: Input, output file and work directory must be distinct
docs.text: Two of the input, the output and the work folder resolve to the same path. Choose a different --work_dir or --output_path.

docs.title: Video preview needs a pretrimmed video
docs.text:
--start and --duration work only for audio input. Either trim the video first, or process its audio:

vexy-speakup run meeting.mp4 --output_path=speech.wav --start=120 --duration=45

docs.title: Set VEXY_SPEAKUP_TTS_ROOT ...
docs.text:
A diarizer, DeepFilterNet or scoring needs the local adapters and the variable is not set, or does not point to a folder. Set it as described in Local models, or run without the adapters:

vexy-speakup run meeting.m4a --diarization_json=turns.json --evaluate=False

docs.title: diarizer must be mlx or sortformer, or supply --diarization_json
docs.text: --diarizer has an unsupported value. Use mlx, sortformer, or supply turns.

docs.title: Errors about turns
docs.text: Message Fix Diarization requires a turns/segments array the JSON must be a list, or an object with turns or segments Turn timestamps must be finite numbers start and end must be numbers, not strings or booleans Turn outside audio duration each turn needs 0 <= start < end, ending within the audio Speaker must be a safe nonempty identifier use only letters, digits, _ and - in speaker IDs

docs.title: Unknown parameter ... use inspect
docs.text:
A chain sets a parameter that the loaded plugin does not have. Names depend on the plugin and its version. Print the real names:

vexy-speakup inspect "/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/Ozone 12 Maximizer.vst3"

Then correct the chain file.

docs.title: Unknown profile ...
docs.text: --profile_name must be dx35, dx65, rx6-dx35, rx6 or bypass.

docs.title: VST unexpectedly silenced input; check license and settings
docs.text: A plugin returned silence for a non-silent fragment. This usually means the plugin is not licensed or activated on this machine, or a setting such as a mix of 0 mutes it. Open the plugin once in a host to check its licence, and check the values in speakers/<ID>/vst-receipt.json.

docs.title: Not an effect
docs.text: The chain loads an instrument or another non-effect plugin. Use an effect plugin, or name the right one in a multi-plugin bundle with plugin_name.

docs.title: A plugin fails to load or times out
docs.text: Each plugin gets 15 seconds to initialise. Each worker process is limited by --timeout (default 1800 seconds). The worker's log, speakers/<ID>/jobs.log or master.log, holds the plugin's output. Raise --timeout for very long recordings.

docs.title: Encoded true-peak limit could not be satisfied
docs.text: After three encodes with decreasing gain, the encoded file still exceeded --true_peak. Use a lossless output such as .wav or .flac, or set a lower --true_peak.

docs.title: AI enhancement changed duration, Assembly changed timeline length, Mastering changed timeline length
docs.text: A processing step returned a different number of samples from its input. The run stops rather than publishing audio that is out of sync. Check the corresponding log in the run folder.

docs.title: The run folder uses too much disk space
docs.text: Every run keeps all its intermediate float WAV files. A long recording can need tens of gigabytes. Delete run folders you no longer need; latest.json names the most recent successful run.
